notes: Retail purchase through the same record model: a receipt Maya imports herself (self_supplied: issuer_id names the shop, but no shop key signs it, so it never becomes issuer_verified) and the matching Bank A card debit txn_9002 (-4599). The receipt's payment_ref NGR-731942 appears in the debit's refs. No RFC is attached; merchant_kid is null because nothing here is issuer-signed. The receipt documents an outflow, so expected.reconciliation counts it with sign -1 (total_pence -4599) against the signed debit (target_pence -4599), and difference_pence is total_pence - target_pence as in schemas.Calculation. alibi.core.reconcile reproduces it with its default signs, where a purchase receipt counts as -1. Synthetic, labelled data: no real people, merchants, accounts or money. Bodies are unsigned: sign merchant events at load time with alibi.fixtures.maya.sign_event and a DemoKeystore, and RFCs with sign_request. merchant_events are pushed by webhook before any RFC; lookup_events are reachable only by follow-up retrieval (settlement_lookup); corrections are pushed later; self_supplied items go through the self-supplied import. Money is integer pence, times are UTC ISO-8601, periods are half-open [from, to). expected is development gold from explicit fields only (statuses, references, amounts, times): statuses lists every acceptable claim status and evidence the revision-pinned refs that decide it. Development and demo data, never holdout.
